Theorem 11.16Terminal absorbers: open

Formalise ordinary and marked transformers and the two alternative wheel decompositions of each resulting absorber. Prove the embedding, avoidance, divisibility and bounded-size conclusions; cite no literature result as a Lean axiom.

Manuscript label: thm:new:ordinary-relative-absorber.

Manuscript label: thm:new:marked-relative-absorber.

Lemma E.311Actual active common-cycle and path counts

Fixed vertex embeddings give exact common-cycle and common-path transport once their free coordinates are restricted to the image. If \(t\) vertices are removed, the cycle loss is at most \(2(m+1)t n^m\) and the canonical path loss at most \(2mt n^{m-1}\). A further physical deletion of active degree at most \(\Delta \) costs at most \(3(m+1)\Delta n_A^m\) and \(4(m+1)\Delta n_A^{m-1}\), respectively. The two root spokes are never imposed on a common path. Compatible-hub loss is at most the number of removed hubs plus \((m+1)\) times the active spoke-row deletion bound. The original and active orders remain distinct in these formulas. Explicit scalar margins turn these comparisons into lower bounds when their displayed numerical budgets hold; the complete cover-down caller must still verify those budgets.

Lemma E.309Actual active cuts and degrees

The sampled typed arc identifiers have exactly the zero-one physical adjacency matrices. Restriction to fixed row and hub embeddings and later physical deletion give all four cut bounds. The cutoff change is explicit: \(1-2\delta \le \kappa (1-2\delta _A)\), where both retained part fractions are at least \(\kappa \). Realized deletion degrees cost \(\zeta \) in the cut coefficient. A rim degree loses at most the number of removed vertices and its relevant physical deletion degree. The incoming marked degree is charged at the shifted physical root. Any change in degree target is charged separately by its absolute difference.

If the final-path interiors are disjoint from the actual residual source graph, the displayed compatible old and residual maps glue to an injection on their complement. The old map need only be injective on the old domain with those interiors removed. The displayed identification of final paths with actually deleted paths gives this domain separation. Lemma E.759Induction over a supplied family of source components

Suppose a finite list specifies, for each factor, ordered source paths and cycles satisfying the stated path or cycle conditions, with vertex-disjoint pieces within that factor. Starting from a valid family state whose unprocessed free vertices are unassigned, the induction processes every listed piece. It preserves all previously assigned images, the common free-image load bound, pairwise disjointness of physical edge sets and the reserved graph condition. Every new image lies in its factor’s specified list. Every listed source arc either has two initially prescribed endpoints or maps to an arc of the target digraph, and every listed source vertex and physical edge is recorded in the final state.

This result is conditional on the displayed list and its hypotheses. The ordered-piece embedding theorem below supplies the final degree and load conclusions. Transport from an arbitrary presentation of the manuscript source graphs, the two preparation callers, and the principal theorem remain to be checked.

Theorem 7.3Concentration for the finite categorical product

For independent finite coordinates \(\sigma _i\), and functions \(a_i\le X_i(\sigma _i)\le b_i\),

\[ \Pr \left(\left|\sum _i X_i-\sum _i\mathbb E X_i\right|\ge t\right) \le 2\exp \left(-\frac{2t^2}{\sum _i(b_i-a_i)^2}\right) \qquad (t\ge 0). \]

The explicit finite product is identified with the product probability measure, proving coordinate independence. The bound follows from mathlib’s proved subgaussian Hoeffding estimate, applied to the centred variables. In a raw directed-colour cut, one physical edge has one categorical colour–direction state. If both directions meet the cut, its two contributions are combined into one \([0,1]\)-valued variable; its expectation is the sum of the two corresponding \(\rho _a/2\) terms. This theorem does not yet establish the simultaneous cut event or its asymptotic failure bound required by the protected partition.

Theorem 8.5Finite independent and hypergeometric Chernoff bounds

Let \(X\) be either a sum of independent finite random variables in \([0,1]\) or \(|S\cap A|\) for a uniform fixed-size subset. Put \(a=\mathbb EX\). For \(0\le \varepsilon \le 1\),

\[ \Pr (|X-a|\ge \varepsilon a)\le 2e^{-\varepsilon ^2a/3}. \]

If \(a{\gt}0\) and \(t\ge a\), then \(\Pr (X\ge t)\le (ea/t)^t\). When \(a=0\), \(X=0\) at every outcome of positive mass. This covers finite random variables; it does not assert a new proof for arbitrary infinite probability spaces.

Lemma 7.9Simultaneous categorical directed-colour cuts

Give each unordered pair one categorical state \((a,b)\) of probability \(\rho _a/2\), where \(\rho _a\ge 0\) and \(\sum _a\rho _a=1\). On graph edges, \(a\) is the colour and \(b\) the direction. The colour classes partition the physical edges exactly. For fixed \(S,T\), their directed-colour count \(X_a(S,T)\) has expectation \(\rho _a e_G(S,T)/2\). For any fixed number of colours \(k\) and \(q{\gt}0\), there is \(N(k,q)\) such that, for every graph of order \(n\ge N(k,q)\) and every such profile, with probability at least \(1-n^{-10}\),

\[ \left|X_a(S,T)-\rho _a e_G(S,T)/2\right|{\lt}qn^2 \quad \text{for every }a,S,T. \]

The threshold precedes the vertex set, host and profile. This absolute quadratic tolerance controls large cuts; it does not replace the separate small-cut argument using vertex degrees in the partition proof.

The product law is explicitly defined and proved to have total mass one. No conditioning on root presence occurs. This does not prove the manuscript-specific identities for physical images or their influence counts.

Theorem 8.3Concentration for independent samples and partitions

Let independent coordinates be uniform subsets or partitions as above. Suppose one exchange in coordinate \(i\) changes \(f\) by at most \(b_i\ge 0\). Put \(s_i=\min (r_i,D_i-r_i)\) for a subset and \(s_i=D_i\) for a partition, and put \(v=\sum _i s_i b_i^2\). Then

\[ \mathbb E\exp \bigl(t(f-\mathbb Ef)\bigr)\le \exp (t^2v/8) \quad (t\in \mathbb R). \]

For \(v{\gt}0\) and \(a\ge 0\), the two-sided tail is at most \(2\exp (-2a^2/v)\), and each one-sided tail is at most \(\exp (-2a^2/v)\). If \(v=0\), \(f\) equals its expectation at every outcome.

Theorem E.3Rounding fractional weights with prescribed local estimates

Fix integers \(r\ge 2\), \(B\ge 1\) and \(K,a,\gamma {\gt}0\). There are \(\eta _0{\gt}0\) and \(n_0\) such that the following holds for \(n\ge n_0\). Let an indexed hypergraph have at most \(n^B\) vertices and edge sizes between \(2\) and \(r\). Suppose nonnegative edge weights \(w\) have vertex loads in \([1-\eta _0,1+\eta _0]\) and pair loads at most \(K/n\). Let \(\mathcal S\) be at most \(n^B\) vertex subsets of size at least \(an\), and let \(\mathcal F\) be at most \(n^B\) fixed functions \(g:E\to [0,1]\) with \(W_g=\sum _e g(e)w(e)\ge an\). There is a matching \(M\) such that

\[ |S\setminus V(M)|\le \gamma |S|\quad (S\in \mathcal S),\qquad (1-\gamma )W_g\le g(M)\le (1+\gamma )W_g\quad (g\in \mathcal F). \]

The thresholds are independent of the number of original edge identifiers.

Lemma 7.8The large-cut consequence of minimum degree

Define \(e_G(S,T)=\sum _{x\in S}|N_G(x)\cap T|\), counting ordered pairs. If \(\delta (G)\ge (1/2+\alpha )n\) and \(|S|+|T|{\gt}(1-2\delta )n\), then

\[ e_G(S,T)\ge (\alpha -\delta )n\min \{ |S|,|T|\} . \]

The count is symmetric in \(S,T\). If \(T\) is the larger side, it has size greater than \((1/2-\delta )n\), and each vertex in \(S\) has at least \(\delta (G)+|T|-n\) neighbours in \(T\). Summation proves the inequality; the other case follows by symmetry. Overlapping sides retain both ordered occurrences of an edge when appropriate.

Definition 1.1Finite graphs and prescribed decompositions

All ordinary graphs are simple graphs on \(\{ 0,\ldots ,n-1\} \). A family \((H_i)_{i{\lt}q}\) partitions the edges of \(G\) if, for every \(u,v\),

\[ G(u,v)\iff \exists i{\lt}q\ H_i(u,v),\qquad H_i(u,v)\wedge H_j(u,v)\Longrightarrow i=j. \]

A decomposition into \((F_i)_{i{\lt}q}\) additionally supplies an isomorphism \(H_i\cong F_i\) for every \(i\). Thus the definition records multiplicities in the prescribed list, spanning vertex sets and exact edge coverage.

Lemma E.53Uniform retention on all fixed restrictions

For fixed \(d\ge 2\), \(p,\zeta {\gt}0\) and real exponents \(C,Q\), there are \(m,N\) such that the following holds. In the original raw interval law on \(|V|=n\ge N\), \(|U|\le n\), the selected start-colour marginal is constant \(t_0\) and \(t_0|U|\ge pn\). Retain only that colour as above. Fix at most \(n^C\) pairs \((S,T)\) with \(S\) permutation-invariant and \(|S|,|T|\ge m\). With probability at least \(1-n^{-Q}\), all raw start counts are within \(n^{3/5}\) of \(t_0|U|/d\), and every row changes at most \(\zeta |S|\) states on \(S\), while every index count changes at most \(\zeta |T|\) states on \(T\), simultaneously for all these pairs. The thresholds precede the host, domains, actual marginal arrays and outcome. The retained law projects exactly to the original raw law, so any other common raw event can be intersected with this event by an additive union bound. Domains must be fixed before exposure.

admit a colouring with \(d\) colours such that two edges of the same colour sharing an endpoint are equal.

Lemma E.17Fixed-profile estimates after deletion

Deleting degree at most \(d\) changes each directed degree by at most \(d\), each directed two-step count by at most \(2d\), and an ordered cut between \(S,T\) by at most \(d\min \{ |S|,|T|\} \). For a bipartite spoke relation, one-, two- and three-column intersections change by at most \(d,2d,3d\). If the fixed inverse-density profile is bounded by \(L\), its weighted row codegrees change by at most \(2L^2d\). Consequently sparse intersection data with error \(\delta \) remain valid with error \(\delta +\rho \), provided \(3d\le \rho |V|\) and \(2L^2d\le \rho |U|\). The supplied profiles and exceptional sets are unchanged, as are the two original normalising domains.

\[ c=\min \left\{ \frac{\varepsilon ^2}{2}, \frac{\gamma ^2p_*^4}{16}, \frac{2\delta ^2}{3(4d+3)^2}, \frac{\delta ^2s_*^4\kappa }{(4d+3)^2}\right\} {\gt}0. \]

The parent degrees must be within \(\delta _Pn\) of \(D\), with \(0\le \delta _P\le \varepsilon /4\), and \(\kappa n\le |U|\le n\). The spoke marginals are fixed and each at least \(s_*\); the ordinary rim marginal is at least \(p_*\). This node does not include the cut or later retention conclusions.

Lemma E.27Ordinary potential loads under the actual raw experiment

Independently sample physical rim edges with fixed supplied probabilities, and sample spokes using the original raw interval law. For ordinary \(r\)-wheels avoiding the permutation conflict graph and fixed coefficients \(0\le w(W)\le Cn^{1-r}\), each root-omitted expected load is exactly the sum of \(w(W)\) times the product of all non-root marginal probabilities. One union-bound event controls all fixed physical rim and spoke roots. On that same event, every later modification of maximum rim and both spoke difference degrees at most \(a\) incurs additional load error at most \(8r^4Ca/n\) for a rim root and \(4r^4Ca/n\) for a spoke root. The seed-specific normalization and distance from the target one are proved in the following node.

Lemma E.28Admissible cycle weights and full-host seed means

Let \(\lambda \) be a nonnegative fractional \(r\)-cycle decomposition of \(P\), with \(\lambda (C)\le C_Pn^{2-r}\), and let \(\Delta (F)\le L\). At an edge \(xy\in E(P)\setminus E(F)\) the weight of cycles containing an \(F\)-edge among their vertices is at most \(5r^4C_PL/n\); at a fixed vertex it is at most \(3r^4C_PL\). In particular \(F_{\pi ,b}\) has maximum degree at most \(2b\). For each admissible cycle and each of the \(m\) hubs use the unchanged coefficient \(\lambda (C)/(mp_R^{r-1}p_H^r)\). Its expected potential rim load equals the admissible cycle weight through the edge. Its expected potential spoke load is \(p_R/(mp_H)\) times the admissible cycle weight through the vertex. If \(p_RD_0=2mp_H\), \(D_0\ge n/2\) and \(|d_P(v)-D_0|\le \varepsilon n\), the two errors from one are at most \(5r^4C_PL/n\) and \(2\varepsilon +12r^4C_PL/n\). The lower and upper seed bounds are \(c_Pn^{1-r}\) and \(C_P/(\omega _*p_*^{2r-1})\, n^{1-r}\), under the manuscript’s supplied size and density bounds. These constants precede \(d\). A single event controls all potential roots with these mean errors plus any prescribed positive deviation \(t\). Its explicit exponential failure bound is eventually at most \(n^{-q}\) for each fixed \(q\). Deleting conflict edges from the physical sample leaves every candidate potential load exactly unchanged.

If at most \(p\) old hubs are active and each has degree at most \(q\), the constructed row and hub sets have total size at most

\[ p\bigl(r(t+5q)+q+2\bigr). \]

This bound does not count unused forbidden vertices.

Lemma 11.4Protected regular edge partition

Fix \(\alpha {\gt}0\), \(k\ge 1\), positive \(r_a,\xi _a\), and an integer \(B\ge 0\). There is \(N\) depending only on these data such that the following holds for every \(n\ge N\). Let \(G\) be an even \(D\)-regular graph of order \(n\) with \(D\ge (1/2+\alpha )n\). Let \(\sum _a m_a=D/2\) and \(\rho _a=2m_a/D\ge r_a\). Fix sets \(I_b\) with \(\sum _b|I_b|\le \alpha n/100000\) before colouring the edges independently with probabilities \((\rho _a)_a\), obtaining \(S_a^0\). With probability at least \(1-n^{-10}\), for every later family of subgraphs \(A_a\subseteq S_a^0\) with \(\sum _a e(A_a)\le B\), there is an exact edge partition \((S_a)_a\) of \(G\) such that

\[ d_{S_a}(v)=2m_a,\qquad A_a\subseteq S_a,\qquad S_a[I_b]=S_a^0[I_b],\qquad \Delta (S_a\triangle S_a^0)\le \xi _a n. \]

The more general checked form protects any fixed graph of maximum degree at most \(\alpha n/100000\), and every later graph of maximum degree at most \(B\).

Lemma 5.3Grouping matchings and recovering physical edges

A \(kq\)-regular bipartite multigraph splits into \(k\) multigraphs with degree \(q\) on both sides. Suppose moreover that its two parts are copies of the vertex set of a simple graph \(G\), and

\[ M(x,y)+M(y,x)=\mathbf1_{\{ xy\in E(G)\} }\quad \text{for all }x,y. \]

Then grouping the perfect matchings into \(k\) groups of size \(q\) and forgetting directions gives an exact edge partition of \(G\) into \(2q\)-regular spanning graphs.

Lemma E.757An ordered path split at prescribed vertices

Lemma E.763Prescribed positions followed by the family embedding

For separately typed source factors represented by vertex-disjoint directed paths and cycles, the source orientation and degree conditions follow from the component structure. Assignment of each physical bad edge to a single factor gives disjoint matching edge sets, and its endpoint occurrences are bounded by its degree in the bad-edge graph. Previously used edges and the reserved graph remain avoided under the stated disjointness conditions. Omitted isolated source vertices can be added as singleton paths without changing arcs or edges.

Lemma 6.1Integral prescribed degrees

Let \(B\) be a finite bipartite multigraph with parts \(X,Y\), whose parallel edges are distinct elements of a finite set. Let \(f:X\to \mathbb N\) and \(g:Y\to \mathbb N\) have equal totals. If

\[ f(S)\le g(T)+e_B(S,Y\setminus T)\qquad (S\subseteq X,\ T\subseteq Y), \]

then a subset of the original edges has degrees \(f\) on \(X\) and \(g\) on \(Y\). The equivalent multiplicity-matrix conclusion also retains every capacity.

Lemma E.751Invariants for prescribed-image embeddings

An injective partial image of a graph of maximum degree two has degree at most two at an image vertex and zero outside its image. For a family of such images, the specified bounds on prescribed and new vertex occurrences yield the stated bound on the union of used physical edges, including the separately forbidden graph. The source-size estimate bounds the sum of the source-factor sizes. Separately, a bound on the actual number of free occurrences gives the stated bound on the number of saturated host vertices; their inclusion in the source family still has to be checked at the caller. A sequence of choices that avoids saturated vertices preserves the stated per-vertex load bound.

One update at a previously unassigned source vertex preserves the earlier images and injectivity if its new image is unused. Adding physical edges to one factor preserves pairwise disjointness if those edges avoid all other factor edge sets. Theorem 6.4Deterministic protected partition

Let \((M_a)\) partition the arcs of a balanced orientation of a simple graph, with total indegree and outdegree \(\sum _a m_a\). Suppose every colour has in- and outdegrees \(m_a\pm e\). Let \(L_a\le M_a\) be its available arcs after protected edges have been excluded. Suppose \(L_a\) satisfies the large-cut bound

\[ e_{L_a}(S,T)\ge h_a n^2\min \{ |S|/n,|T|/n\} \quad \text{if }|S|/n+|T|/n{\gt}1-2\delta _a, \]

and

\[ 0\le e{\lt}q\le \min _a m_a,\quad 0\le \delta _a{\lt}1/4,\quad \frac{2e}{q-e}\le \delta _a,\quad q+e\le h_an/2. \]

Then the underlying graph has an exact edge partition into \(2m_a\)-regular graphs. Each colour changes at most \(4q+2e\) edges at any vertex. Every edge unavailable for deletion in all colours retains its original colour.

Lemma 7.6Fair orientations and simultaneous two-step paths

Sample one fair bit for each unordered vertex pair; bits on nonedges are unused. This gives exactly one direction to each edge. For a fixed eligibility graph \(E\subseteq G\), the number of directed paths \(x\to z\to y\) with both edges in \(E\) has mean \(|N_E(x)\cap N_E(y)|/4\). For \(x\ne y\), different choices of \(z\) use disjoint physical coordinate pairs. The probability of at most \(|N_E(x)\cap N_E(y)|/8\) such paths is at most \(2\exp (-|N_E(x)\cap N_E(y)|/64)\). The corresponding degree bounds and all pair bounds hold on one event with the explicit sum of their failure bounds. On this event, the routing conclusion holds for every later forbidden graph satisfying its degree bound.

Lemma E.25Permutation windows and raw interval geometry

The ambient permutation window \([-a,b]\) has at most \(a+b+1\) labels, with equality when the permutation has no sufficiently short cycle. Distinct isolated starts have disjoint successor-extended intervals. The raw state at \(x\) reads activation coordinates in \([-2d,d]\), start colours in \([-d,0]\), and the original colour at \(x\). Both the number read and the number of label states that can read any coordinate are at most \(4d+3\). Labels at permutation distance greater than \(3d\) have disjoint coordinate supports.

Lemma E.26The original raw interval law

Use the activation law \(a_d=1/(2d+1)\), isolated-start probability \(r_d=a_d(1-a_d)^{2d}\), start-colour probabilities \(q_g/(dr_d)\), and original label-colour probabilities \(s_j/\overline q\), where \(\overline q=1-(1+1/d)\sum _gq_g\). For \(d\ge 2\) and \(\sum _gq_g\le 1/8\) and \(\sum _js_j\le \overline q\), with nonnegative \(q_g,s_j\), all these laws are valid. Suppose the permutation has no cycle of length at most \(2d\). A label receives interval colour \(g\) with probability \(q_g\), is outside all extended intervals with probability \(\overline q\), and receives ordinary colour \(j\) with probability \(s_j\). States at separated labels are independent; the entire vectors at distinct hubs are independent. These are the raw states before uniform retention, whose law is not asserted to be a product law.

Lemma E.29Common-neighbourhood counts in the raw experiment

For a fixed label set \(A\) and a nonempty fixed hub set \(J\), count labels in \(A\) receiving the selected ordinary colour at every hub in \(J\). Its mean is \(|A|\prod _{u\in J}s_u\). Its deviation at \(t{\gt}0\) has probability at most \(2\exp (-2t^2/((4d+3)^2|J|n))\). One event gives the corresponding estimates for any specified finite family of fixed domains and hub sets. Applying it to \(A=V\) and \(A=N_P(v)\) for every ambient vertex \(v\) gives the sizes of the actual random common neighbourhoods and every degree into them. The vertex \(v\) is not required to belong to the random neighbourhood.

Theorem 5.1Perfect matchings in a regular bipartite multigraph

Let \(X,Y\) be finite sets and \(M:X\times Y\to \mathbb N\) the edge multiplicity function of a bipartite multigraph. If every row sum and column sum is \(d\), there are bijections \(\sigma _c:X\to Y\), indexed by \(c{\lt}d\), such that

\[ M(x,y)=\sum _{c{\lt}d}\mathbf1_{\{ \sigma _c(x)=y\} }. \]

When \(d=0\), the index set is empty; no equality of the sizes of \(X,Y\) is required in that case.

Lemma 1.8Concentration of the remaining colour degrees

Let \(U\) be a clique in the line graph of a hypergraph of rank at most \(k\) and codegree at most \(B\). For each edge in \(U\), consider its resource cliques other than the clique defining \(U\). For a fixed colour, count the uncoloured edges satisfying lower bounds on the numbers of these cliques where that colour was assigned and rejected. The coordinate certificates have maximum weight at most \(2+(k+3)kB\) and total weight at most \((3+3k)|U|\).

The actual remaining colour degree is the alternating sum of the diagonal and next-diagonal counts. The formal result gives a mean-centred tail bound by applying the proved certificate inequality to these counts.

Lemma E.24Local dependence for fixed root-omitted patterns

Let fixed nonnegative coefficients weight finite resource patterns, and omit the tested root resource from each product. If the total coefficient at a root is at most \(L\), each remaining pair weight is at most \(a\), and each pattern has at most \(q\) remaining resources, the sum of squared resource influences is at most \(aqL\). If each resource reads at most \(B\) independent primitive coordinates and each primitive coordinate belongs to at most \(B\) resource supports, the squared primitive influence sum is at most \(B^2aqL\). Consequently the two-sided deviation probability at \(t{\gt}0\) is at most \(2\exp (-2t^2/(B^2aqL))\) when this supplied variance bound is positive. Exact expectations factor when the non-root resource supports in each pattern are disjoint. Restriction to any fixed injective subfamily of primitive coordinates preserves its product law.

Lemma E.52Conditional retention and state changes

For a fixed raw outcome, put \(A_a=\{ u:a\text{ is a retained raw start of the selected colour at }u\} \) and \(t=\min _a|A_a|\). Independently over \(a\), choose a uniform \(t\)-subset \(J_a\subseteq A_a\). For \(W\subseteq A_a\),

\[ \Pr (W\cap J_a=\varnothing )\le \left(\frac{|A_a|-t}{|A_a|}\right)^{|W|}. \]

A deleted start changes at most \(d+1\) states, in its interval and successor. For a permutation-invariant set \(S\), only starts in \(S\) can change states in \(S\). At a fixed vertex, only the \(d+1\) possible preceding starts can change its state. If every raw start count differs from its common mean \(\mu \ge pn/d\) by at most \(n^{3/5}\), the deletion probability is at most \((4d/p)n^{-2/5}\) for sufficiently large \(n\).

Lemma E.30Dense conflict-free sets with prescribed roots

Fix \(s\) prescribed roots, a positive density margin \(\alpha \), and a positive neighbourhood-size proportion \(\beta \). Definition 1.11The two target propositions

For a \(2\)-regular graph \(F\), allowed component lengths are encoded by

\[ \forall v,\quad |\{ w:v\text{ is connected to }w\text{ in }F\} |\in S. \]

Write \(\mathcal D(S,\alpha ,n)\) for the conclusion of the main theorem at these parameters, universally quantified over the even degree \(D\), the family indexed by \(\{ 0,\ldots ,D/2-1\} \) and the \(D\)-regular host. The fixed-set target is

\[ \forall S\ne \varnothing \ \forall \alpha {\gt}0\ \exists N\ \forall n\ge N, \quad \mathcal D(S,\alpha ,n), \]

and the uniform target is

\[ \forall \alpha {\gt}0\ \exists N\ \forall S\ne \varnothing \ \forall n\ge N, \quad \mathcal D(S,\alpha ,n). \]

In both formulas, \(S\subseteq \{ 3,4,\ldots \} \). These are definitions of propositions, not proofs of either proposition.

Lemma 1.7Concrete tentative-colouring counts

A vertex tentatively chooses a colour and a colour-dependent retention coin. It retains the colour if the coin succeeds and no neighbour chose that colour. The retained colours form a proper partial colouring. All one-root and independent-set joint retention probabilities are computed in the original product law. For lists of size \(l\), let \(N(v,c)\) be the number of neighbours with \(c\) in their lists. If \(N(v,c)\le K\) whenever \(c\) belongs to the list at \(v\), the coin probability \((1-1/l)^{K-N(v,c)}\) makes the retention probability at every vertex exactly \((1-1/l)^K\).

For a clique \(T\), the number of rejected vertices has coordinate certificate weights at most \(2\) and total at most \(3|T|\). For a family of \(k\) vertex sets and a fixed list \(L\), let \(M(a,b)\) count colours in \(L\) assigned in at least \(a\) sets and rejected in at least \(b\) sets. This count has certificate weights at most \(1\) and total at most \(3k|L|\). Lemma 11.9Four-cycle lower bound and local threshold comparisons

We have \(\delta _4\ge 2/3\). For \(t=4k+7\), take cliques \(A,C\) of size \(t\) and an independent set \(B\) of size \(t-1\), add all \(AB\) and \(BC\) edges, and delete a six-cycle inside \(C\). Definition 1.2Ordinary cycle thresholds

An embedded \(r\)-cycle is specified by an injection from \(\{ 0,\ldots ,r-1\} \) whose consecutive pairs, with indices taken modulo \(r\), are precisely its edges. Other ambient vertices are isolated. A \(C_r\)-decomposition partitions edges into such embedded cycles. A graph is \(C_r\)-divisible if all degrees are even and \(r\) divides its number of edges. Define

\[ \begin{gathered} \delta _r=\inf \{ d\in [0,1]:\exists N\ \forall n\ge N\ \forall G,\\ \ G\text{ is }C_r\text{-divisible},\ \delta (G)\ge dn \Longrightarrow G\text{ has a }C_r\text{-decomposition}\} ,\\ \delta _S=\sup _{r\in S}\delta _r. \end{gathered} \]

Theorem E.1Uniform weighted matching with fixed relative error

Fix integers \(k\ge 2\), \(B\ge 0\) and real numbers \(K,a,\gamma {\gt}0\). There is \(n_0\) such that the following holds whenever \(n\ge n_0\) and \(n\le D\le n^B\). Let \(\mathcal H\) be a finite indexed \(k\)-uniform hypergraph with no isolated vertices, at most \(n^B\) vertices, maximum degree at most \(D\) and maximum codegree at most \(KD/n\). For a family of at most \(n^B\) functions \(w_i:E(\mathcal H)\to [0,b_i]\), where \(b_i{\gt}0\), put \(W_i=\sum _e w_i(e)\) and suppose \(W_i\ge a b_iDn\). There is a matching \(M\) such that

\[ |w_i(M)-W_i/D|{\lt}\gamma W_i/D \qquad \text{for every prescribed }i. \]

The threshold is chosen before the hypergraph and the weight functions.
